events.title: Sport Climbing Camp
events.short_description: For the Rockbusters team climbing is not just a sport, it’s what we eat, drink, breathe and sleep - it’s what we live for. Our Sport Climbing Camp gives you the opportunity to get a taste of what we mean and become part of our climbing crew. Come and join us for a week or two in one of the best European crags. You’ll get to spend all day on the face, taking on as many climbs as your fingers can handle. Then, it’s all back to camp to kick back and relax as hard as you want to - living the climbing life we love.

children.text: During the Sport Climbing Camp we’ll provide one-on-one coaching, video and photo analysis to help improve your performance. This is really useful for climbers who already have some outdoor experience and who want to hone their technique and to get deeper into the climbing culture.
During your stay you’ll get:
On-going performance coaching so that you’re always building on your technique
Time on slab and vertical ground to improve footwork for better climbing
Work on balance so that you climb in a more efficient way (leading F5 or more)
Overhang work to build strength and confidence so you can take on tougher climbing challenges
Tuition for difficult routes of F6 or more for more experienced climbers looking to move up the grades
Red point and on-sight attempts so you can tackle new climbs more easily

The focus of our Sport Climbing Camp is on quality climbing, so it’s aimed at climbers with some experience. Beginners might be more suited to our Novice course, which is equally intense but in a different way. We will push you to achieve more during your stay,arming you with all the necessary techniques and safety measures before you try anything new.

You’ll be shown how to use a guidebook so you can read the topo and figure out new climbing areas for yourself. We’ll develop your calls and communication so you can stay in touch with other climbers on the face, and communicate with those at the base. You’ll learn about cleaning anchors and safe belaying for top rope and leading. Basically, everything we know we’ll try and pass on to you. And that’s a heck of a lot.
Our Sport Climbing Camp gives you a little glimpse of what it’s like to lead the climbing life. This is who we are and what we do, and we’d love the chance to show just why we do it every day. .

events.title: Sport Climbing Course: Kalymnos, Greece
events.short_description: Two weeks of intensive coaching on some of Europe's best limestone — tufas, pockets, and enough quality routes in your grade to actually feel the improvement by the time you fly home.
events.comparison_intro: One week gets you the Kalymnos initiation. Two weeks means real progression — enough time to actually feel the improvement stick.

children.text: Shared accommodation in local climbing hostels, cottages, or places run by local climbers. Want something more comfortable? Send us a personal inquiry by email or WhatsApp.
Fly into Kos, then a short ferry across to Kalymnos. Local transport on the island is organised once you land.

events.trip_detail_travel_note: Fly into Kos — we handle the rest

children.text: Kalymnos is basically what happens when a Greek island decides to be made entirely of climbable limestone — steep walls, hanging tufas, and stalactite features that turn every route into a three-dimensional puzzle.

Two weeks of daily coaching from Sergi and Miha, covering everything from proper belaying and clipping tactics to redpoint mindset and overhang technique — whatever's actually holding your climbing back.
Small enough group ratios (max 7:1) that you're never just another face in the crowd, big enough energy that the evenings are just as memorable as the days.
Maximum climbing time, minimum logistical hassle. Coaching happens on the rock, not in a classroom.
08:30 — Morning Briefing Crag plan, conditions check, coffee
09:30 — Guided Climbing Block Movement & technique coaching on selected lines
13:00 — Crag Lunch & Reset Packed lunch, rest, tactics chat with your coach
14:30 — Afternoon Session Project burns or mileage — your call
18:30 — Pack Down & Return Back to base, gear sorted for tomorrow
20:00 — Dinner & Debrief Greek food, cold drinks, and tall tales from the day
All safety equipment provided — ropes, draws, helmets, slings. Bring your own shoes and harness if you have preferences; we've got spares if you don't.
5–8 participants, max 7:1 coach ratio. Minimum 3 to run the course — otherwise we offer an equivalent alternative or a full refund.
No stock photos, no staged sends — just climbers earning it on Greek limestone.

A small Dodecanese island that quietly became one of Europe's best sport climbing destinations — steep grey limestone dripping with tufas and stalactites, set right above a genuinely turquoise Aegean.
Routes here reward technical, three-dimensional movement over raw power, with a huge spread of grades packed into a small area — ideal for a course built around real, measurable progression.
Nearest Airport: Kos (ferry transfer)
Rock Type: Limestone
Climate in October: 20–27°C
Style: Steep tufas & technical pockets

events_audience_cards.body: You're comfortable indoors at 6a, but outdoor leading still feels like a completely different sport. Two weeks of guided mileage fixes that gap fast.

events_audience_cards.body: Technically fine but stuck at the same grade for way too long. Sometimes it just takes someone watching you climb to see what you can't.

events_coach_team_bullets.text: Sergi Medina — Performance Coach. Born and raised around Barcelona's best crags — Montserrat, Siurana, Margalef — Sergi has been climbing for 25 years and now splits his time between Greece and Spain, leading courses and trips across both.

Miha Popovic — Performance & Mental Coach. A late starter who progressed to onsighting 7c within three years, Miha left a career in research writing to become a certified climbing instructor and guide, bringing a genuinely science-minded approach to coaching mental barriers.

faqs.question: What level do I need to be?

children.text: Previous outdoor sport climbing experience is highly recommended, at a minimum of indoor leading 6a or outdoor leading 5. This course suits climbers from strong beginners to advanced, and it's open to ages 15 and up.

faqs.question: Do I need my own gear?

children.text: Bring climbing shoes and a harness you trust. We provide belay devices, helmets, and slings, plus a full kit list once you book (down jacket, headlamp, sleeping bag, and a backpack for crag days).

Breakfast and lunch ingredients are covered — we take you shopping on arrival, and there's an equipped kitchen at the accommodation. Dinner is flexible: communal dinners can be organised, or head to one of the many nearby restaurants and bars.

faqs.question: What if fewer than 3 people book?

children.text: We need a minimum of 3 participants to run the course. If numbers don't add up, we'll offer an equivalent (or better) alternative trip, or a full refund. No hard feelings.

faqs.question: Can I book just one week?

children.text: Yes — each week runs individually at €1,090. This page covers the full 2-week option at €1,890; see the schedule above for single-week dates.

faqs.question: Where do I fly in and out of?

children.text: Kos International Airport, followed by a short ferry crossing to Kalymnos.

reviews.quote: I'd been stuck at the same grade for two years. Two weeks with Sergi and I finally understood what my feet were supposed to be doing. Embarrassingly simple fix, huge difference.
Came alone, left with a group chat that's still active a year later and three trips already planned. The climbing was great. The people were the real upgrade.
Miha's video analysis showed me things about my climbing nobody had ever pointed out before. I onsighted my project route on the second-to-last day.
